chunks: Ismaʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام:
That ʿAlī عليه السلام was appealed to in a dispute concerning a man who had taken a runaway slave, and he remained with him, then escaped from him.

He said: "He is to swear by Allah, besides Whom there is no god, that he did not strip him of his clothes, nor anything from what was upon him, nor sell him, nor collude in sending him off. Then if he swears, he is cleared of liability."

key_terms.آبِقاً: a runaway slave who has fled from his master
key_terms.إِرْسَالِهِ: his release or letting him go
key_terms.سَلَبَهُ: he took from him or stripped him of property

ai.seo_question: When is a person not liable after a runaway slave escapes from his custody?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding liability when a person takes custody of a runaway slave who later escapes. Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled that if the person swears he neither took the slave’s property, nor sold him, nor facilitated his escape, then he is absolved from financial liability.
